question.problem:
If the function $f(x)={log}_{2}⁡(\frac{x-1}{5})-k$ has an inverse function given by

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=5\cdot {2}^{x-3}+1,
$$

what is the value of $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{2}⁡(\frac{x-1}{5})-k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{5})-k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{5})-k \\ {log}_{2}⁡(\frac{y-1}{5}) & =x+k \\ {2}^{{log}_{2}⁡((y-1)/5)} & ={2}^{x+k} \\ \frac{y-1}{5} & ={2}^{x+k} \\ y-1 & =5\cdot {2}^{x+k} \\ y & =5\cdot {2}^{x+k}+1\end{aligned}
$$

    

Therefore, the inverse function is ${f}^{-1}(x)=5\cdot {2}^{x+k}+1.$ 

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-3.$
